GIS plays a vital role in enhancing planning, improving operational efficiency, and supporting evidence-based service delivery within municipalities, while also enabling compliance with key legislative frameworks such as the Municipal Systems Act (No. 32 of 2000), Municipal Structures Act (No. 117 of 1998), Spatial Data Infrastructure Act (No. 54 of 2003), and the Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act (No. 6 of 2004). During the 2014/2015 financial year, the municipality developed a GIS web portal as a public-facing viewer that allows users to access spatial i

ks, including the Municipal Systems Act (No. 32 of 2000), Municipal Structures Act (No. 117 of 1998), Spatial Data Infrastructure Act (No. 54 of 2003), and the Local Government: Municipal Property Rates Act (No. 6 of 2004) by ensuring the effective management, sharing, and utilization of spatial information. In addition, the upgraded portal seeks to provide a reliable and sustainable solution for hosting and maintaining geospatial data and applications, ensuring improved system performance, data security, and long-term accessibility aligned with current technological standards. OBJECTIVES OF THE PROJECT The objective of these terms of reference for a GIS web portal project is to appoint a qualified and experienced service provider to design, upgrade, implement, and maintain a secure, scalable, and user-friendly web-based GIS platform for the Winnie Madikizela-Mandela Local Municipality. The service provider will be responsible for upgrading the existing portal, updating and maintaining the spatial information available on the system, incorporating new datasets where necessary, and hosting the portal and its data on a reliable external platform for a period of three (3) years, with payments made on an annual basis.
